messages:
evans_sales: Hey team, Evans Corp (POC) asked for a quick checklist. They want Private deployment into their AWS account. Questions: PrivateLink vs VPC peering which we recommend, do they need a bastion/Jumphost for agent install, minimal firewall ports, and any pricing delta for dedicated egress vs shared?

ajay_neteng: tl;dr: PrivateLink for single-account, peering for low-latency multi-VPC within same region. If customer wants strict egress control + no cross-account hostability PrivateLink is better.

sam_solutions: Also depends on DNS+routing preferences. PrivateLink = interface endpoints, we recommend a small ENI & endpoint in their spoke VPC. Peering needs route table entries and won't work cross-region.

evans_sales: They specifically asked about agent install access — can we avoid a bastion?

kyle_infra: You can avoid a bastion if their ops team allows SSM Session Manager to the worker nodes. Otherwise an ephemeral bastion (jumpbox) is the simplest path for onprem installers. :thinking_face:

liz_security: Security checklist: must allow outbound HTTPS to our control-plane IPs (we provide a CIDR list), open 443 to the endpoint. If using PrivateLink, enforce endpoint policy and restrict access to service principals. Audit logs must be forwarded to their SIEM.

ajay_neteng: Firewall ports minimal: 443 outbound to our endpoint or public egress, 22 only if they insist on SSH (prefer SSM). If using peering, allow intra-VPC traffic 10.0.0.0/16 -> our service subnet.

sam_solutions: Pricing: Private deploy + VPC endpoints has a small per-hour endpoint cost on AWS + data processing charges. There is no extra per-token charge but dedicated capacity (Reserved) adds monthly fee. We should surface rough numbers.

evans_sales: Can you give a short sample security snippet we can send to their network team?

liz_security: Sure — send this: ```
# Allowlist for Private Deploy (example)
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to: 34.198.12.0/24, 52.23.89.0/24 (redwood control plane)
- If using PrivateLink: create Interface Endpoint to com.redwood.inference, restrict with endpoint policy to account 123456789012
- Block inbound from public internet to service subnets
- Forward VPC flow logs to their log collector (s3/kinesis)
```

kyle_infra: For onprem NAT/proxy setups: ensure TLS passthrough or allowlist the FQDNs; we try to avoid TLS-intercept. Also recommend MTU 1500 for initial tests; lower later if they have tunnels.

ajay_neteng: One gotcha: if customer terminates TLS at their proxy and inspects, PrivateLink still works but session preservation needs SNI passthrough. Call out in runbook.

sam_solutions: Action items for sales handoff: 1) ask for their account ID + VPC CIDRs, 2) decide PrivateLink vs Peering, 3) ops contact for SSM/Jumpbox decision, 4) security contact for endpoint policy + log retention.

evans_sales: Great — I'll send the snippet + ask for account ID and ops contact. Any blockers on our side for GA features?

ajay_neteng: No blockers. If they need cross-region we'll propose a multi-endpoint setup and route via our smart routing (costs increase).

deploybot: Deployment note: template available: `templates/privatedeploy/aws/1-quickstart.yaml` — can run `./deploy.sh --account <id> --region us-east-1` after IAM role is in place. :robot_face:

sam_solutions: I'll draft the POC SOW bullets (networking + security + pricing) and share in this thread when ready.

evans_sales: Thanks all — will update once I have account ID and ops contact. :thumbsup:
